news.title: Martin appreciates 'clarity' over Foxes ownership
news.summary: Leicester City manager Russell Martin says he appreciates owner Khun Aiyawatt "Top" Srivaddhanaprabha going public with his decision to take the club off the market.
body: Leicester City manager Russell Martin says he appreciates owner Khun Aiyawatt "Top" Srivaddhanaprabha going public with his decision to take the club off the market.
Earlier this week the Foxes' Thai chairman confirmed that the League One side is no longer up for sale and that there will be a "refocus" on rebuilding the side after years of decline.

Martin, who addressed reports about the development last week, said he hopes Khun Top's open letter will allow everyone to "draw a line under" ownership talks which have swirled around the club since it dropped into the third tier after back-to-back relegations.
"Clarity on any situation is really good and I'm really grateful to the chairman for providing it," Martin told BBC Radio Leicester.
"The best thing is that you don't have to ask me about it every press conference and we can move on from that.

"It maybe stops a bit of external noise around the ownership of the club and the club being sold and being told there is a deadline every other week and it's not been met, and then someone's buying the club and people doing interviews on Talksport saying they want to buy the club and all the stuff.
"I don't think that is very helpful for us, if people listen to that. So I think it stops all of that really and what will be will be now."
You can listen to more from Martin, the abandoned sale of the club and BBC Radio Leicester's preview of the Foxes' League One game against Mansfield Town by hitting the play button above.

news.title: Gateshead loan Plymouth's Roberts and Leicester's Gray
news.summary: Caleb Roberts has played 10 times for Torquay United in National League South this season
body: Caleb Roberts has played 10 times for Torquay United in National League South this season
Gateshead have signed Plymouth Argyle midfielder Caleb Roberts and Leicester City defender Kevon Gray on short-term loan deals.

Roberts, 21, who joins until 3 January, made 10 appearances while on loan at National League South side Torquay United earlier this season and played in the National League on loan with Truro City at the back end of last season.
He has made three first team appearances for Plymouth this campaign which came in the Carabao Cup and Jersey Mike's Trophy.
Gray, 19, who will be with Gateshead until 24 December, signed a three-year contract with the Foxes in March and made his Championship debut against Blackburn Rovers in May.
Meanwhile, Gateshead have confirmed that defender David Ferguson has left the club to join Spennymoor Town on a permanent deal.

news.title: Leicester City team news vs Mansfield with exit decision looming for defender
news.summary: Christian McFarlane is likely to require surgery on an ankle injury sustained during the international break, Leicester City manager Russell Martin has revealed.
body: Christian McFarlane is likely to require surgery on an ankle injury sustained during the international break, Leicester City manager Russell Martin has revealed.

The left-back returned from England Under-20s duty earlier this month after featuring twice for Darren Moore's side. He played 10 minutes in a 6-1 win over the Czech Republic before making a short cameo against Portugal four days later.

Martin ruled McFarlane out of the games against Huddersfield Town and Blackpool last week , revealing that the club were awaiting a second opinion on the injury. Now, the Leicester boss has confirmed that surgery is required, with talks to be held with the defender's parent club, Manchester City, about his future.

"Still Christian, who's going to need an operation, unfortunately," Martin said when asked about the latest team news. "So we'll have a discussion with Man City early next week about what the short-term future looks like for him, but it's highly likely right now he'll have an operation which will rule him out for a bit of time.
"So it's probably in everyone's best interest that he goes back there and assesses his situation after that. But we'll have to wait and see."

He added: "He's done something to his ankle playing for England, so really unfortunate. He didn't come on for very long and there's damage to the ligaments in his ankle. So nothing that's going to harm him long-term at all, it's a pretty standard procedure, but it's really unlucky and I really feel for him.

"He came in, did really well, picked up a couple of little injuries and then the times where he would have had game time to get back into the swing of things would have been the international break. He's been called up despite a a lack of game time here and then unfortunately, he's got injured. So sometimes football can be hard for players, but he's a great young man and a really good player."
Christian McFarlane has suffered an injury (Image: 2026 Plumb Images)

Will Smallbone is another player unavailable for Leicester , with the midfielder sidelined until after Christmas. Smallbone has played six times for the Foxes since signing in October but suffered a muscle injury early in the win over Huddersfield.

After missing this week's draw against Blackpool, the 26-year-old is now expected to miss the rest of 2026, but will return before the end of the season. "I don't think we need to put any pressure on Will about timelines and stuff," Martin said when asked about specific return dates.

"I think it won't be this side of Christmas and I don't think it'll be the first couple of weeks in January and then we'll assess it again after that. But he'll definitely be back to play some part for us. Like I said, I think you can see what he's brought on the pitch - he's already scored.

"He brings so much quality and composure and understanding of what we're after in a couple of positions. Yeah, unfortunately for us, it's a big loss. And really unfortunate and really bad luck for Will.
Smallbone suffered an injury against Huddersfield (Image: Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

"He's had a really tough time over the last couple of years of injury and sometimes that's part of the journey. I've got no doubt at some point he'll get fit and he'll stay fit. He'll be a huge player for us.
"So, yeah, really disappointed for him and for us. And now we just have to make sure when he comes back that he's really right and ready to help us."
Jayden Joseph is back fully fit after coming off the bench in the last two games, while Jakub Stolarczyk and Ben Nelson remain the two long-term absentees at the King Power Stadium.

news.title: Leicester City investment approach revealed as fan favourite explains what happened
news.summary: Former Leicester City striker Steve Howard has revealed that he first became aware of King Power's attempt to sell the football club more than a year ago.
body: Former Leicester City striker Steve Howard has revealed that he first became aware of King Power's attempt to sell the football club more than a year ago.

King Power and the Srivaddhanaprabha family placed the club on the market earlier this year after US investment bank Citigroup produced a sales brochure setting an asking price of more than £200m for the League One club.

The change in direction at the King Power Stadium came on the back of consecutive relegations that saw Leicester drop from the Premier League to the third tier for just the second time in the club's 142-year history.

This week, Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha confirmed that the club was no longer for sale after failing to attract a buyer. "We recently undertook a structured process to explore whether new investment or a change of ownership could actually be the right thing for the club," he said in an open letter to supporters.
"Those discussions have not resulted in an agreement, and I have decided to conclude the process to enable us to refocus on the work needed to move the club forward."
Following the ownership's U-turn, Howard joined the When Your Smiling podcast on BBC Radio Leicester to discuss what the decision means for the club.

During the conversation about King Power's ownership, the former striker revealed how he first heard about a potential change in direction more than 12 months ago. Howard also shed light on two interested parties who approached him before the sale process became public in July.

"I got a whiff of this probably a year ago," he told BBC Radio Leicester. "I was asked if I could find some investors for the club and I went through that process where I would try to talk to possible investors.
King Power have taken City off the market (Image: Getty Images)

"Yes, they were interested, and all of a sudden it went public, which I just thought myself was a bit bizarre because if you want something lucrative and a bit exclusive, you don't want everybody to know about it. I think putting the club on the market was a bad move for the ownership, if he wanted to sell it.
"He was trying to do the best for the club, get another investor to take it further. He's obviously put it up for sale, he's gone, 'there you go, that's what I want for it'.

"He's asked for far too much money and all the investors say, 'well why would I buy that when there's better options in the Championship and it'll cost a quarter of the price'. He's thought to himself that he's not going to get the asking price, let's backtrack. Let's see what [I can do] moving forward with King Power and I just thought, that's just a get out."

He added: "I was approached by two investors asking whether I could get a meeting with the owners to entertain investment or to buy the club. We're talking about a year ago. So I tried and I tried, it wasn't sitting right with certain people and certain people didn't want to say if the club was for sale or if it wasn't, because they had signed NDAs.

"King Power and Top [were] just asking for too much money for the football club. As an investor, take your heart out of it and go in with your head, you ain't buying Leicester City [for that price], you're not."

news.title: 'Start them both' - Leicester City given answer to Jayden Joseph and Will Alves selection headache
news.summary: Will Alves and Jayden Joseph have been two of Leicester City's standout players this season in League One. The academy graduates have stepped into the first team and impressed under Russell Martin.
body: Will Alves and Jayden Joseph have been two of Leicester City's standout players this season in League One. The academy graduates have stepped into the first team and impressed under Russell Martin.

Joseph returned from his loan spell with Tranmere Rovers and cemented his place at right-back in City's defence, while Alves has played across the attack. But the change of formation last month means fitting them both into the same team is a tricky prospect.

During Joseph's injury absence, Alves shone at right wing-back and established himself as one of Martin's best performers this season. However, Joseph is now back and has been part of the matchday squad for the past two games.
So, against Mansfield Town on Saturday, how do Leicester line up to fit them both back in? Or does Alves drop out for Joseph to start from the off?
In our latest LeicestershireLive fan panel, we asked supporters how they want to see the Foxes look with the pair.
Darren says: "This has created a dilemma with Joseph returning from injury and arguably our best player this season and Alves currently playing right wing back.

"I think the only way they can both play in the team together is returning to four at the back, with JJ right-back and Alves in front of him. This obviously means a change in formation, and I can’t see Martin going back to this, as the formation they are currently playing is what he looks more comfortable with due to the unbeaten run.
Will Alves scored a sensational goal for Leicester City vs Blackpool (Image: 2026 Plumb Images)

"I personally feel, watching Joseph come on in the last two games, that he looks a little rusty, which is expected after a long injury. I would start him on the bench against Mansfield and bring him back slowly, which will create competition for the place, which is what is needed with a squad.
"Looking ahead, we also have some cup games coming up and perhaps start with JJ and get him back up to be fully match fit. It’s a nice dilemma to have."
Adam says: "Now we have Joseph back fit again, it's going to be a tough job for Martin to fit him into a reasonably settled starting 11.

"For me, there is one player he could replace while still giving the XI some tactical flexibility, and that person would be Caleb Okoli . The Italian hasn't looked comfortable at times this season with the ball at his feet and does seem to put a lot of fans on edge when he's under pressure.
Caleb Okoli of Leicester City during his side's game against Blackpool (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

"With JJ replacing Okoli, that would then see Thomas come into the back three at LCB, JJ in the RWB role and Alves in the LWB role, which he played on Tuesday night in the second half against Blackpool, when he netted. This move would certainly give Leicester the tactical flexibility to go to the back four should he want to."

Jacob says: "I think Alves has done a solid job in the RWB role and equally as well last night at LWB, getting a goal as well. But I think there is an argument for him to play more centrally, specifically in the role which Kamari Doyle and Sammy Braybrooke played in.

"I wouldn’t be opposed to seeing Alves replace Doyle on Saturday, as I think Alves brings faster-paced decision-making than Doyle does. Start them both! McCarthy, Joseph, O’Hora, Souttar, Okoli, Thomas, Lundstram, Page, Braybrooke, Alves, Riis."
Eli says: "Jayden Joseph comes straight back into the starting XI, but Will Alves needs to be playing further forward.

"Joseph offers us natural defensive ability, pace and energy at right-back, allowing us to return to a more balanced back four. However, I don’t think we should sacrifice Alves to accommodate him. Will has taken his opportunity in Joseph’s absence, performed exceptionally well and deserves to keep his place.
"For me, the solution is to play Joseph at right-back and move Alves into one of the attacking midfield positions, where he can influence games further up the pitch.
Jayden Joseph and Will Alves (Image: 2026 Plumb Images)

"Alves has shown that he has the ability to carry the ball, take players on, create opportunities and cause opposition defences problems. Those are qualities we need more of, particularly against teams who sit deep and make it difficult for us to break them down.

"I’d rather see us find a way to get our best young talents into the same starting XI than create a situation where one has to miss out. Joseph at right-back, Alves further forward. It’s a win-win situation for Leicester, and potentially a very exciting partnership for the future."

news.title: Leicester City academy notebook: Transfer interest, international star and 17-year-old U21s captain
news.summary: Leicester City's academy teams have been busy across various competitions in recent weeks, with the Under-21s and Under-18s enjoying mixed success in league and cup action.
body: Leicester City's academy teams have been busy across various competitions in recent weeks, with the Under-21s and Under-18s enjoying mixed success in league and cup action.

The Under-21s continue to feature players who have earned the opportunity to train with Russell Martin's first-team squad , alongside some of the club's most exciting teenagers. Matt Rains' Under-18s provide the perfect bridge for the likes of Bismark Owusu and Jake Fletcher to make the step up to the Under-21s.
This week's academy notebook includes the Under-18s' FA Youth Cup progress, Premier League interest in one of Leicester's most exciting youngsters and more...
Make sure you never miss the latest Leicester City news and opinion by making Leicestershire Live one of your Google preferred sources
Despite sitting bottom of the Premier League U18 North table, having played just seven games compared with the nine or 10 by other sides, City's Under-18s have been in fine form in the FA Youth Cup.

Rains' side beat local opponents Anstey Nomads 4-1 in the first round , thanks to a scintillating second-half display, to set up a tie against MK Dons. On Friday, they produced another impressive performance to run out 4-0 winners.

David Anugo, Hugo De Lisle and Owusu, three players who regularly feature for the Under-21s, were among the scorers at Seagrave. Rollo Szembel also got on the scoresheet, with the midfielder finishing well from close range.

Jon Rudkin and James McCarron watched the win from the training ground, with Under-21s coach Adi Yussuf and right-back Bade Aluko also present. Rudkin and McCarron have regularly attended academy fixtures this season and were also at Anstey for the first-round tie, as was Martin.
Szembel and Owusu scored for the Under-18s against MK Dons (Image: 2026 Plumb Images)

Leicester's youngsters will face Stockport County, whose academy also holds Category Three status, in the third round. A date for the tie is yet to be confirmed, but all matches must be played by Saturday, December 12.
City face Sunderland (November 28), Everton (December 5) and Derby (December 12) in the league before that deadline, so the trip to Stockport is expected to take place in midweek between those games.

The Under-21s suffered defeat in their penultimate Premier League Cup game at Bournemouth on Monday night. Last week, City beat Plymouth Argyle at Home Park to move within touching distance of the next stage.

Leon McSweeney's side played their part in an entertaining encounter at Wimborne Town as the Cherries won 5-3. Bournemouth were 2-0 up inside 16 minutes before Riley Carr scored a brilliant individual goal to halve the deficit.

The young Foxes had a number of chances to equalise, but the home side restored their two-goal lead before the break. Striker Josh King made it 3-2 after half-time, only for Bournemouth to score twice in three minutes and put the game beyond Leicester's reach. Lorenz Hutchinson converted a penalty shortly afterwards, but the Foxes were unable to get back on level terms.
FOLLOW ON FACEBOOK! All the latest Leicester City news on LeicestershireLive’s Leicester City Facebook page
Get the best Leicester City news, analysis and more straight to your Inbox!
To get it, it's a simple one-two punch.

After five games, Leicester are third in Group B and level on points with Cardiff City, who sit above them on goals scored. The decider will take place at Seagrave on December 4, with City hoping to repeat their 3-1 win in the reverse fixture in October.

Premier League clubs have scouts travelling up and down the country in search of the next up-and-coming star. For clubs battling to secure the best young talent, Leicester's academy and Seagrave are a goldmine.

Owusu has impressed whenever he has featured for the Under-18s and has made four appearances for the Under-21s this term. In the 4-0 win over MK Dons, he was a constant threat down Leicester's left and capped his performance with a goal.
Owusu was superb for Leicester City Under-18s in the FA Youth Cup (Image: Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

Now, his potential appears to have attracted interest from a number of clubs. Pete O'Rourke has reported that Leeds United and Brentford are both eyeing a move for the winger, with Parma, Utrecht and FC Copenhagen also interested in the Ghanaian.

City are keen to keep hold of their most promising academy players. Trey Nyoni and Tyrese Noubissie both left for nominal fees to Liverpool and Manchester City respectively, and the club will be keen to avoid a repeat. Those within the club have made the pathway from academy to first team clear and they will be hoping Owusu is another player they can develop themselves.

Since pre-season, Riley Carr has been catching the eye for City's academy and has also impressed Russell Martin. On his senior debut against Stevenage, he looked sharp and dangerous during his 70 minutes on the pitch before experiencing the FA Cup against Oxford City.
Carr is impressing for Under-21s and Scotland Under-19s (Image: 2026 Plumb Images)

The winger received his first call-up to the Scotland Under-19s squad this month and featured in all three of their European Championship qualifying games. Carr started in victories against Kazakhstan and Kosovo before playing 25 minutes off the bench in the 4-1 defeat to Belgium.

There has been more individual recognition, this time for Michael Toko. The 17-year-old centre-back is a regular for the Under-21s and captained the Foxes in their 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest.

Having been with the club since the Under-14s, Toko has worked alongside Kevon Gray and Alpha Diallo in the heart of the young Foxes' defence. Alongside De Lisle, David Anugo and Fletcher, he has also helped the Under-18s progress in the FA Youth Cup.

His performances haven't gone unnoticed, either. Martin watched him closely in pre-season, named him in the squad against Genoa back in August and has had him part of his senior group in parts this season. He has also received recognition from outside the club.

Leicester City's academy teams have been busy across various competitions in recent weeks, with the Under-21s and Under-18s enjoying mixed success in league and cup action.

Matt Rains' Under-18s provide the perfect bridge for the likes of Bismark Owusu and Jake Fletcher to make the step up to the Under-21s.

This week's academy notebook includes the Under-18s' FA Youth Cup progress, Premier League interest in one of Leicester's most exciting youngsters and more...

news.title: Leicester City chairman Khun Top speaks out on OH Leuven future in statement
news.summary: Leicester City chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha has reaffirmed King Power's commitment to OH Leuven after the family ended its attempts to sell its footballing assets.
body: Leicester City chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha has reaffirmed King Power's commitment to OH Leuven after the family ended its attempts to sell its footballing assets.

Khun Top's future at City and OH Leuven had been in doubt since the summer, when it was reported that King Power were looking to sell both clubs and other assets. However, no agreement was reached with potential buyers, with the £200m valuation understood to have been a stumbling block.

On Wednesday, Top penned an open letter to Leicester supporters following CEO Kevin Davies' decision to step down. The Thai businessman confirmed that Leicester City are no longer for sale, with the club set to "refocus" on rebuilding after a sharp decline.

Top has also reinstated King Power's commitment to OH Leuven, who the family purchased in 2017. In an open letter to the Belgian club's supporters, the 41-year-old reiterated his family's commitment to the Pro League side.
FOLLOW ON FACEBOOK! All the latest Leicester City news on LeicestershireLive’s Leicester City Facebook page

"Dear supporters, Almost ten years ago, a special story began for my family and King Power in Leuven," the letter read. "A story in which we experienced many beautiful moments together and in which OH Leuven underwent a wonderful development.

"From promotion to the top division of Belgian football to the development of OH Leuven as an established first-division club. From OH Leuven Women's two national titles and fantastic European campaigns in the UEFA Women's Champions League to the progression of various young talents from our own youth academy. Together, we have built a professionally structured club with strong foundations and great ambitions. These are achievements of which we are particularly proud.
King Power bought OH Leuven in 2017 (Image: Philippe Crochet / Photonews via Getty Images)

"With the future of our football clubs in mind, King Power has recently explored opportunities for new investments, including at OH Leuven. That process has now been concluded without an agreement being reached. This changes nothing regarding our commitment to OH Leuven. King Power continues to support the club and will work together with the management to further strengthen the club, both on and off the pitch. Our ambition remains to build a professionally managed and competitive club.

"OH Leuven's financial position remains secure thanks to the support of King Power. That support will be continued. At the same time, we continue to work towards a more financially sustainable club, with sufficient stability to realize our sporting ambitions and to continue growing in the long term. We are proud of what we have achieved in recent years, but want to take further steps in the coming years.
"My family and I remain committed to the future of OH Leuven. I would like to thank you for your continued support and involvement with the club."

news.title: Leicester City set for Christian McFarlane loan talks with Man City after injury blow
news.summary: Leicester City and Manchester City are set to discuss Christian McFarlane's loan spell in January after the left-back was ruled out until the New Year.
body: Leicester City and Manchester City are set to discuss Christian McFarlane's loan spell in January after the left-back was ruled out until the New Year.

McFarlane joined the Foxes in July on a season-long loan to provide back-up to Luke Thomas. The 19-year-old has made six appearances in all competitions but has played just three minutes since October 6.
Martin started McFarlane in the 2-1 defeat to Stevenage in the Jersey Mike's Trophy, but the defender was subsequently left out of every squad until the FA Cup clash at Oxford City.
He was then ruled out by the Leicester boss ahead of the Huddersfield game.
"We have Christian McFarlane, who got injured and looks to be out for quite a while, which is a real shame for us and for him," Martin said ahead of the Huddersfield game.
"He's had a few [injuries], it's been a bit of a stop-start. He's had a couple of injuries.
"He's had quite a bad one on his ankle, so we need a second opinion on that to see if he needs an operation or not, which is a big disappointment."
McFarlane has suffered an injury that will keep out for a period of time (Image: 2026 Plumb Images)

On Tuesday, Martin confirmed to LeicestershireLive that the England Under-20s international, like Will Smallbone, would be sidelined until at least Christmas, with discussions to follow between Leicester and his parent club over his future.

"I think we won't see him this side of Christmas," he revealed. "Then it will be a discussion between us, him and Man City about what the plan is and whether he ends up staying and trying to get fit and get back in the team here, or if he ends up going back there.

news.title: EFL Trophy holders Luton face Palace U21s in last 32
news.summary: Jersey Mike's signed a five-year sponsorship deal with the EFL in September
body: Jersey Mike's signed a five-year sponsorship deal with the EFL in September
Holders Luton Town will host Crystal Palace Under-21s in the last 32 of the Jersey Mike's Trophy.
The Hatters, who beat Stockport County 3-1 in last season's EFL Trophy final at Wembley, won their group in the opening stages of the competition, coming through their three matches unbeaten.
Three-time winners Peterborough United have been drawn away at Plymouth Argyle with Posh hoping to win the trophy for a record fourth time.
Wycombe Wanderers have been handed a potentially attractive tie at home to Arsenal's U21s while Leicester City visit Barnet.

In the northern section, last year's runners-up Stockport will face League Two strugglers Port Vale while Wigan Athletic and Doncaster Rovers, who have both won the competition twice will meet at The Brick Community Stadium.
Managerless Blackpool, who have also won the trophy on two previous occasions have been drawn away at Notts County.

news.title: Leicester no longer for sale as owner refocuses on future
news.summary: King Power, the Thai business that Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha is part of, bought Leicester for £35m in 2010
body: King Power, the Thai business that Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha is part of, bought Leicester for £35m in 2010

Leicester City owner Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha has confirmed the one-time Premier League title winners are no longer up for sale and there will be a "refocus" on rebuilding the side after years of decline.

The Foxes were put on the market in the summer after back-to-back relegations saw the side drop from the Premier League and straight through the Championship to land in England's third tier for just the second time in the club's 142-year history.

A sales brochure was produced by US investment bank Citigroup in which an asking price of more than £200m was put on a League One club that a decade ago had defied all expectations by winning the Premier League title at 5,000-1 odds.

Leicester never publicly acknowledged that the club had been put up for sale, with under-fire chief football officer Jon Rudkin going so far as to say he "cannot comment on speculation" when asked about it in a rare interview with BBC Radio Leicester in October.

Khun Top, however, has now said that there were no takers when investment had been sought for a side that the Srivaddhanaprabha family, through its King Power duty free business in Thailand, have owned for 16 years.

"We recently undertook a structured process to explore whether new investment or a change of ownership could actually be the right thing for the club," Khun Top wrote in an open letter to Leicester City supporters on the club's website. , external
"Those discussions have not resulted in an agreement, and I have decided to conclude the process to enable us to refocus on the work needed to move the club forward."
'Business as always' - Foxes boss Martin brushes off sales talk
Listen to BBC Radio Leicester's When You're Smiling podcast
Follow Leicester City on BBC Sounds
Pre-match, post-match and topical Foxes content

Three relegations in four years, having yo-yoed between the Premier League and Championship before going down to League One, has badly damaged the relationship between the Foxes' owners and their supporter base.

While a golden age of success was bankrolled by King Power, with Premier League glory in 2016 followed up by FA Cup success in 2021, high spending on an underperforming side in recent years has led to an increasing number of supporters calling for Khun Top to sell up.
But the Thai businessman said he has a "deep connection" to Leicester and "its people".

And it is not just euphoric sporting moments that have forged the bond he is talking about, as his father - and predecessor as Foxes chairman - Khun Vichai died in a helicopter crash outside the stadium in 2018.
"For my family and me, Leicester City has been a big part of our lives for many years," he said.
"We have experienced extraordinary moments together, as well as some very difficult ones."
Khun Top added that the struggles of recent years, which included the club being hit with a points penalty last season for breaking spending rules, has got him "thinking a lot about our direction".
Earlier this year he told BBC Radio Leicester that he shoulders the blame for the club's decline.
"Making better decisions" as well as "continuing to learn from our past experiences" are two steps the club "need to take", he said.
Khun Top has insisted that through King Power, a company that has endured difficulties in recent years, the club's "financial position remains secure".
However, he added that there was "work needed to put Leicester City on a more sustainable footing".

"That has been a principle behind the work and decisions of the last year – giving the club the appropriate support for its immediate circumstances, while building the organisational discipline and financial resilience that will underpin a responsible plan for future growth," he said.
As part of Khun Top's missive, he confirmed that chief executive Kevin Davies will be stepping down from the role in December.
Davies had only been in the job since March, and was promoted to the position after a shake-up of a number of leadership roles.
